findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/61-twenty-first-after-pentecost/sections/20-armour-under-providence.tex:291-304 (third objection; proof p. 20), sections/40-last-exodus-of-the-church.tex:226-243 (second objection; p. 29) and sections/50-comparison.tex:68-92 ('Where they differ'; p. 31)
findings.problem: This recurs within the advisory filed at iteration 0, which named the Hilary-Augustine difference on the Communion as argued three times. Iteration 1 reduced the two readings' versions to pointers. The STU-011 repair has expanded them again into full accounts of four witnesses. Each of the three passages now names, in near-identical words, Hilary's present power and 'not the judgment of the resurrection', Augustine's martyrs and the Church's persecutors, Bellarmine's 'wicked who persecute and tempt', and Cassiodorus joining 'the devil with his ministers' to 'the judgment at the end of the world'. Each then says the Fathers 'differ in what is asked and in whom the plea names, not only in the time' and that the answers are 'compatible, not identical' through Thomas's 'instruments moved by the devil'. That is about 120, 170 and 250 words; 40 and 50 share 34 eight-word sequences. Every account is now accurate. A reader reading straight through meets the same comparison three times in twelve pages, which works against the profile's 'one fullest home'.
findings.required_result: Keep the full account of the four witnesses in 50-comparison.tex only. In each reading's objection, state that reading's own answer and the chief contrary one in a sentence or two, without dropping a qualification that makes them true: what is asked and whom the plea names differ, not only the time, and the answers are compatible but not the same. Then point to the comparison. Do not reintroduce any claim that the witnesses agree on the persecutors or on the thing asked.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/61-twenty-first-after-pentecost/research/scope.md 3.5 (Bellarmine entry, 'stands against Augustine's Enarr. 89.2', line 483), 4.7, 7.4 and 11 item 3; src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/61-twenty-first-after-pentecost/research/interpretations.md 4.1 (line 674, 'Gregory and Aquinas serve readings 1 and 3')
findings.problem: This stands unchanged from iteration 1, because neither research record has changed (both hash-match the seal). The scope record files Bellarmine 'For Moses' and 'against' Augustine on Ps 89. It omits his Preface II §5 ('perhaps even more likely, that all of the Psalms are by David, as Saint Augustine maintains', text.txt line 63) and his Davidic reading in the Ps 89 exposition. Interpretations 4.1 has Aquinas serve readings 1 and 3, but he serves all three (Super Matth. 18, per ingratitudinem, in reading 2). The study states both correctly. The concise and homily components reference these records, and scope 7.4 states what 'the studies may say' of Ps 89.
findings.required_result: On the research record's next revision, add Bellarmine's Preface II §5 and his Davidic reading of Ps 89 to scope.md. Recast him there as admitting Moses' authorship as tenable while preferring David's, which places him with Augustine except on whether Moses is admissible. Correct interpretations.md 4.1 to say that Aquinas serves all three readings.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/61-twenty-first-after-pentecost/sections/20-armour-under-providence.tex:291-298 ('Hilary asks for power in this life ... what the prophet now asks'; 'The Fathers differ'; p. 20) and sections/40-last-exodus-of-the-church.tex:236-243 ('The Fathers differ'; 'without making it the only one'; p. 29)
findings.problem: The rewritten sentences have three small slips. (1) 'The Fathers differ' follows lists that include St Robert Bellarmine, a Doctor, and in 40 also Cassiodorus. Neither is a Father: author-standing-v1.toml records Bellarmine as 'doctor' and Cassiodorus as 'ecclesiastical-writer'. (2) In 20 the same sentence says both that 'Hilary asks for power in this life' and 'what the prophet now asks'. In Hilary's text the prophet prays (dari sibi id potestatis orat) and Hilary expounds, so the reader cannot tell who is asking. (3) 40 ends with 'This reading follows the end-directed answer ... without making it the only one'. The clause tells the reader the study's own stance, a form the 1962 profile excludes ('Do not tell the reader ... that the guide has declined to press an inference'), and the paragraph has already shown the other answers. None of the three misstates a witness's position.
findings.required_result: Say 'the witnesses differ' (or name them) in place of 'the Fathers differ' where Bellarmine or Cassiodorus is included. In 20, make the prophet the one who asks in Hilary's reading (for example 'In Hilary's reading the prophet asks for power in this life ... and what he now asks is not ...'). Delete 'without making it the only one'.

summary: Cold re-review of the research-edition study of the 1962 Twenty-first Sunday after Pentecost (main.tex and its nine sections). All 21 sealed inputs hash-match REVIEW_INPUTS. A fixed-point rebuild in scratch is byte-identical to the author proof (37 pages, SHA-256 9a690e1d...). A word diff against the iteration-1 proof located every change: STU-011's repair in 20-armour-under-providence.tex, 40-last-exodus-of-the-church.tex and 50-comparison.tex, the Gospel cross-reference in 10-each-element.tex, the timestamp and contribution in generation-metadata.tex, and the iteration-2 entry in research/production-review.md. STU-011 is cleared. Each witness is now credited only with his own answer, and each answer was checked at source: Hilary, PL 9 cols. 573-574, Caph 5 (tracked text layer lines 45950-45990: 'Non illud utique quod in resurrectionis saeculo meminit futurum'; the devil and his ministers; the power of Lk 10:19); Augustine, Enarr. 118.84-88 (NPNF1-8 lines 58205-58262: the martyrs' words, 'when vengeance shall fall upon Her persecutors', 'nothing save the truth'); Bellarmine on Ps 118:84-85 (text.txt line 4295: 'judge and condemn those that persecute and tempt me'); Cassiodorus, Expositio 118, v. 84 (monumenta.ch web text, read 2026-10-15: 'id est diabolo cum ministris ... celeritatem futuri iudicii'); and Aquinas, Super Eph. 6 lect. 3 (1857 OCR lines 37755-37779: 'actio quae instrumento attribuitur', 'a superiore movente, sc. a diabolo'). 40 no longer credits the comparison with an agreement it does not state, and 50's persecutors row and 'Where they differ' paragraph now agree with both readings. STU-007 is cleared by its second option: the cross-reference now states what 30-debt-forgiven-from-the-heart.tex gives (the denarius as a day's wage and Augustine's Sermon 83.3 reckoning). Consequential-difficulty test, the Communion's plea in readings 1 and 3, run at the loci above: the inferences are reported accurately and the prose teaches the question, so the test passes. Hilary's few days lead to a present power; Augustine's order of the two questions leads to 'until the judgment'. The production audit's iteration-2 word counts match detex (each element 4,536; readings 3,811, 3,587 and 3,022; comparison 1,458), and its dispositions are honest. Generation metadata matches the run header and the dispatched effort. Three readings remain, each engaging all ten elements, each with its own four senses and two developed carrying Fathers. Unchanged components were not re-derived. Limits: the PG 27 exposition, PL 26, Rupert, Durandus, Honorius, Sicard and Schuster's other loci were checked only through the research records (Schuster p. 181 on the Communion was read). Verdict PASS, with no blocking finding. Four advisories: STU-005 (recurred), STU-012 (carried), STU-013 and STU-014.
